description:

Content the spec item must capture:

1. Data source (settled): L7 draws from the CURRENT (classic) reconstruction engine — reconstruction_*.ts, the one that already feeds the row-based viewer — NOT the layered engine (layered_*.ts, which feeds /api/layered-graph -> layered-app, a different page from layer1.html). 2. Coverage rule: EVERY parsed record type gets a node — every row in the conversation log is drawn on the timeline. Rows the engine classifies as ignorable are hidden by default via a header toggle '[✓] hide ignored nodes', ON at page load. This explicitly REPLACES an earlier draft's 'no-node-ever ruling for session/meta records' — there is no such ruling; they get nodes, the filter just hides them when ignorable.

3. Tool call / tool result: two SEPARATE nodes (not one collapsed node as the old app does), connected by a dashed bracket so the pairing between a tool_use node and its tool_result node is visible.

4. Presumption promotion (a rule for EVERY layer, not L7-exclusive — must be worded as cross-cutting, matching DECISIONS.md): whichever layer can resolve a presumed node — because no nodes occur between it and its surrounding beacons — promotes it to verified. This is new behaviour: today nothing ever promotes or demotes a presumption node (listGapsBeforeVerifiedNode, layered_end_state.ts:24-32, only ever inserts presumedUserEdit gap nodes, never resolves them).

5. Explicit non-scope: script execution results are entirely L6's; L7 owns no slice of them. Also explicit boundary with S20/L3: Write body, complete Read echo, and Edit's originalFile all collapse into L3's 'extracted edit' scope, NOT L7 — state this so S22 does not re-model what S20 already owns.

6. Session annotation track (settled answer to the placement question): user prompts, agent responses, and the ~54k non-file metadata rows get a NEW shared annotation track on the same ruler — they are NOT duplicated per touched file. This is genuinely new UI: every content-bearing widget in layer 1 today is file-scoped (buildStagePairs/buildOrphanBucket, layer1-widgets.ts:71,89); the only existing session-level element is a 7px coloured bar with a tooltip (renderSessionRanges, layer1-widgets.ts:83-92) — not a lane, carries no content. 7. Rewind rendering (settled, ties directly to L5/S-item-not-yet-written but must be restated here since it resolves an L7 node-type question): NO rewind node, and NO code-vs-conv inference. A rewind renders as dimmed nodes plus a dashed elbow in the bubble, per plans/mvp-app-mockup.html layer 8 — the same visual the L5 branch-rendering mockup will use once built. State the hard fact plainly: a code rewind is NOT derivable from the transcript. Verified against the real s7-minimal-code-restore JSONL: AttachmentPayloadType (vocabulary.ts:55-71) has no restore/checkpoint/rewind member; s7 contains zero edited_text_file attachments across 45 attachments; file-history-snapshot versions simply increment across the rewind with no reset or restored-to marker; the ONLY trace is that the post-rewind prompt shares its parentUuid with the pre-rewind prompt — structurally identical to an ordinary conv-only rewind (the same fork signature findRewindPoint, reconstruction_branch.ts:85-86, already uses). Do not let S22 claim a synthetic edited_text_file surfaces a restore — that earlier plan-prose claim is refuted by the real data.

8. Unknown record types + stampless-timestamp rule (settled): unrecognised record types render as a '[?]' catch-all node (not a throw/closed-list design). A record with no timestamp takes the PREVIOUS stamped record's timestamp (equal-to-previous, not an average and not +1ms) — this matches the task-224 precedent's reasoning of avoiding 'inventing an instant that no evidence supports' (implementation-notes-tasks-223-224-...:107-111). State that the three currently-conflicting code behaviours should converge on this one rule: drop (viewer_api_layer1_sessions.ts:25-27), sort-first (views/timeline-line-nodes.ts defaults `when` to \"\" which string-sorts above every real timestamp; views/reconstruction-coverage.ts:84-86 keys a stampless gap to 0), sort-last (viewer_api_records.ts:83-86). Cite the real volume: ~22% of records in the RevEng project (42,790 of 192,303) carry no timestamp, almost entirely session metadata (last-prompt, permission-mode, custom-title, agent-name, bridge-session, mode, file-history-snapshot, ai-title, fork-context-ref) — every content-bearing type (user/assistant/attachment) carried a timestamp in every sample, so this rule governs metadata volume only, not the nodes users actually look at. State plainly that worktree-state (124 hits) and relocated (87 hits) are REAL record types already present in real logs and ABSENT from the RecordType enum — the [?] catch-all is not hypothetical, there are already 211 unknown-type records in the real corpus today.

9. Reference vocabulary for the spec item to enumerate (so the [?] fallback and the 'every record type gets a node' rule are grounded): full RecordType vocabulary at vocabulary.ts:4-21 + parse/recordKeys.ts — user, assistant, system, attachment (14 AttachmentPayloadType kinds incl. edited_text_file, hook_success, diagnostics...), fileHistorySnapshot, fileHistoryDelta, lastPrompt, mode, permissionMode, bridgeSession, aiTitle, customTitle, agentName, queueOperation, forkContextRef; sub-vocabularies BlockType, ToolName, EventKind, Verdict, GitOperationKind, BranchRole. Old-app comparison baseline for what a 'node' can look like: TimelineNode union (views/timeline-types.ts:216) — user-turn/agent-turn, session-end, commit, tool-call, jsonl-line.

10. Fixture discipline: viewer_api_layer7_fixture_data.ts per the one-file-per-layer convention. Must include at least one record of an unknown type (e.g. modeled on worktree-state or relocated) rendering as [?], and at least one stampless record whose rendered position equals the previous stamped record's timestamp, to exercise the approximation rule.

Verify section: every parsed record type in the fixture produces a node; '[✓] hide ignored nodes' is checked at load and hides rows the engine marks ignorable, unchecking reveals them; a tool_use/tool_result pair renders as two nodes joined by a dashed bracket; a presumed node with no nodes between it and its surrounding beacons auto-promotes to verified; a rewind fixture scenario renders as dimmed nodes + a dashed elbow with no separate rewind node anywhere in the DOM; the session annotation track renders prompts/responses without duplicating them onto any file bubble, and the render mechanism is demonstrably windowed (does not brute-force render every row at once — assert only viewport-scoped DOM nodes exist, not a literal 54k-row count in the fixture); an unknown-type fixture record renders as [?]; a stampless fixture record's screen position matches the previous stamped record's, not an averaged or offset instant.

title: Write spec item S24 — Layer 9: ruler range export to a jfred git branch
description:
Write S24 into specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md, after S23. Layer 9 in task #340's plan — commit mode, the only layer that WRITES. Source: plans/340-recon/L9-ruler-range-export.md (SETTLED section — all eleven ambiguities closed) and plans/340-recon/DECISIONS.md. Follow S20's shape. This item must open by noting it AMENDS earlier S16/S17 text on the same page (segment/patch generation) rather than replacing it wholesale — S16/S17 already cover per-file at-or-before snapping and segment-to-git-diff concatenation; S24 narrows and changes the segmentation model and adds the actual commit step.

Content the spec item must capture:

1. Not a layer: like L8, L9 adds no node kind — it is a MODE the user arms (arming enables cut marks on the ruler), not a checkbox in the show row.

2. The model change (this is the load-bearing correction — state it as amending S16/S17, not restating them): the OLD text 'n marks -> n+1 contiguous segments covering the whole ruler' is REPLACED by a growing-prefix model: one marked range = one segment = one commit. The first commit's base is the commit chosen by a NEW ruler base marker. Each LATER commit's base is the jfred branch's own tip (not the ruler base again). The user may stop at any time — full ruler coverage is never required. The user may NOT start a range in the middle — chunks only ever extend the prefix from the base forward. Skipping a stretch does not omit it: because each commit diffs the jfred tip against the new mark, anything in the skipped interval is absorbed into the next commit, and that commit's message must say so, in the literal form 'includes N unmarked changes.'

3. The jfred branch itself: forks from an EXISTING commit on the timeline, chosen by the new ruler base marker — never an orphan root, never current HEAD. Created LAZILY, on the first commit only (not on arming). The base is IMMUTABLE once chosen; changing it requires deleting the jfred branch entirely and re-arming. Append-only: no amend, no reset, no force-push, ever — deleting the branch is the ONLY undo, so the tool never rewrites history it did not just create itself. HIDDEN from the repo's branch picker via a one-line filter in buildLayer1RefsView (viewer_api_layer1_refs.ts:41-53, which runs `git for-each-ref refs/heads` today with no exclusions) — this is the single exclusion point, so a reconstruction can never accidentally be loaded against the synthetic branch. Note for the spec item: jfred/docs/ui-component-glossary.md currently has NO 'Branch picker' row at all — that gap should be named as something this work must fix, not silently left.

4. What may go in a commit (v1 scope, hard constraint): a marker may ONLY be placed on a BEACON node. No derived node may ever carry a marker. State the reasoning: this is what makes 'any jfred commit counts as a beacon on the next pass' sound rather than self-certifying — every committed byte was independently verified before it could be committed, so a later pass extending the branch can safely treat the commit itself as new evidence. Each file in a chunk contributes its NEAREST VERIFIED STATE AT-OR-BEFORE the mark (this restates S16/S17's per-file snap rule, unchanged); a file with nothing verified yet by that point is absent from the commit until its own first beacon. Per-file snap variance (i.e., which file snapped to which earlier instant) is written into the commit message. Bytes are PINNED at mark time, not re-read at commit time — what the user saw on the timeline when they placed the mark is exactly what lands in git, even if something upstream changes before the commit actually runs.

5. Dates: author date = the mark's instant (always a real evidenced moment, since v1 restricts markers to beacons); committer date = wall clock at export time. The commit message carries a footnote in the literal form 'reconstructed by JFRED @ <real timestamp>'.

6. UI surface: jfred commits render in a DEDICATED STRIP BESIDE THE RULER — a genuinely new render surface with its own layout, hit-testing, and scroll sync; nothing renders on the ruler itself today. v1 is COMMIT ONLY — no multi-file patch export in this item; the existing per-file patch download stays exactly where it already lives (exportPatch, layer1-diff-pane.ts:140-152), unchanged.

7. What already exists, reusable as-is (name these so the spec doesn't ask for a rebuild): per-file unified diff via runGitUnifiedDiff (src/render_git_diff.ts:19, `git diff --no-index`, strips the preamble down to hunks) reached through buildLayer1DiffPayload (viewer_api_layer1_diff.ts; GET /api/layer1-diff + POST /api/layer1-diff-content). A git-apply-able patch shape already exists client-side only: exportPatch() (layer1-diff-pane.ts:140-152) wraps hunks with synthetic `diff --git`/`---`/`+++` headers into a downloadable Blob, per file, per pane — there is no multi-file concatenation and no server-side `git apply` anywhere yet. The range gesture already exists for exactly two instants: shift-click two lane nodes triggers extendDiffSelection -> a `.diff-wash` band + createDetailViewsForFiles(view, files, {baseInstant, targetInstant}); resolveRangeStepIndexes (layer1-diff-wash.ts:31-50) ALREADY implements the per-file at-or-before snap, just for 2 instants — this needs generalizing to n commits under the growing-prefix model (snapping only to n-commit/n-disk/n-snap kinds, NEVER n-created). Verified byte sources already dispatch by kind: readLayer1FileBytes (viewer_api_layer1_file.ts:55-62) handles commit (git show), disk (readFileSync + escape check), and snapshot (sidecar) forms; `.n-created` is the existing no-bytes node kind the drawer already refuses to open (`:not(.n-created)`) — this is the direct precedent for 'refuse a marker that lands on an unbacked/derived node.'

8. What does NOT exist yet (name the real gap plainly): zero `git commit`/`git apply`/`git branch`/`checkout -b` calls anywhere in src/ today — every git spawn in the engine is currently read-only. New write calls should follow the existing argument-array spawnSync pattern used by the read-only calls, not shell string interpolation.

9. Thin adapters needed: an arming-state + mark-placement branch inside layer1-ruler-click.ts (makeRulerTickClickable, layer1-ruler-click.ts:74-92, currently single-click-only: expand row or scroll to bubble — no drag gesture exists); the generalized resolveRangeStepIndexes described above; a server-side per-file-per-segment diff loop plus concatenation, reusing exportPatch's header-wrapping logic moved out of the pane and onto the server; a new route that performs apply-and-commit (`git apply` then `git commit --date` per segment, strictly in order); the one-line branch filter in buildLayer1RefsView; a new ruler-strip node class and placement logic for jfred-branch commits (the first render surface of its kind).

Verify section — because this is the one layer with real filesystem/git side effects, the verify section must go beyond DOM assertions (name this explicitly in the spec item; the recon docs do not prescribe a test harness for the write path, so flag that whoever builds this must run verification against a throwaway/scratch git working tree, never the user's real repo, consistent with how other engine tests in this project already isolate git state): arming the mode shows a cut-mark affordance on ruler ticks; placing a mark succeeds only on beacon-backed nodes and is refused (with a visible reason) on a derived or `.n-created` node; a first commit's base is exactly the ruler-base-marker commit, verified by `git log`; a second commit's base is the jfred tip, not the original ruler base, verified by parentage; skipping a stretch between two marks produces a commit message containing 'includes N unmarked changes' with the correct N; author date on each commit equals its mark's instant and committer date equals wall clock, both checked via `git log --format`; the message footnote 'reconstructed by JFRED @ <timestamp>' is present; the jfred branch is created only after the first commit (not at arming time) and never appears in the repo branch picker dropdony; deleting the jfred branch is the only way to change its base, and doing so allows re-arming against a new base; concatenated per-segment patches `git apply --check` cleanly in sequence; the new ruler-adjacent commit strip renders one entry per jfred commit with independent scroll sync from the node lanes; the existing per-file patch download still works unchanged.

Acceptance: S24 is written into specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md, follows S20's structural shape, opens by stating it amends (not replaces) the existing S16/S17 segment/patch text, and contradicts nothing in DECISIONS.md — in particular it must not describe the old 'n marks -> n+1 segments covering the whole ruler' model, must not allow a marker on a derived node, must not allow amend/reset/force-push on the jfred branch, and must not add jfred to the visible branch picker.

Depends on: Amends the existing S16/S17 spec text on the same page rather than being independent; the recon doc's 'growing prefix' model must be reconciled with, not appended alongside, the older segment/patch wording already in specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md.

title: Engine build-out: Layer 3 beacons and extracted Edit/Write nodes
description:
Spec item S20 in specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md (rewritten 2026-07-30) is the source of truth for WHAT to build; this task is the engine + webapp implementation behind the #343 mockup, not a restatement of it.

Engine must compute/expose, per S20's three stages: (1) Read tool results carrying full contents -> beacon; (2) Bash results carrying full contents (Bash(cat FILE) and friends) -> beacon, Bash stays excluded as a *change* source; (3) Edit/Write events applied onto the immediately preceding beacon -> provably verified beacons via structuredPatch base->target. Add buildEditDerivedNode beside buildNodeFromEvent (jfred/src/layered_load.ts:99-109) so an edit event emits the new L3 node kind instead of collapsing to a byteless preAnchorStub -- LayeredNodeKind (jfred/src/structures/vocabulary.ts:125-131) currently has exactly five members (beacon, preAnchorStub, endState, presumedUserEdit, scriptRun) and none carries hunks. Replay stays lazy, triggered by node click: walk back to the nearest preceding beacon, replay any unpopulated intermediate nodes first (firstHunkMatchesBase / applyEdit, jfred/src/reconstruction_replay_edit.ts:155-168, both in-memory), and classify the result verified (matches the next beacon) or derived (does not). The one disk-touching step -- the BackupReader stale-base fallback (editBaseIsStale / staleEditSeedFor, jfred/src/reconstruction_reseed.ts:22-38,127) -- is a per-HTTP-request read, copying the existing shape of readSnapshotFileContent -> createSidecarReader (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_snapshot.ts:66-73); a backup-seeded node renders as the 'reseeded' confidence state, one of the seven states settled in DECISIONS.md (never a bespoke marker). New NDJSON progress endpoint runs the existing extractFileEvents (jfred/src/reconstruction_extract.ts) over the configured sessions and joins each event's absolute target to a pair via relativizeToProjectFolder (jfred/src/layer1_snapshot_wire.ts:16-23) -- the same join snapshots already use -- firing the first time the [3] preset OR its show-row checkbox becomes visible, per the visibility-triggers-computation rule in DECISIONS.md, scoped to nodes in the rendered viewport.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: new wire field edits? on WirePairOf (jfred/webapp/layer1-wire.ts:26-35, the snapshots? precedent), placed via listPairLadderInstants / listOrphanLadderInstants (jfred/webapp/wire.ts:96-109); a new appendEditNode + .n-edit class in jfred/webapp/layer1-widgets.ts; a describeNode branch in jfred/webapp/layer1-drawer.ts:38-53 reading the existing data-session-id/data-session-file/data-line attribute contract (appendSnapshotNode, layer1-widgets.ts:27-37) so JSONL Nav flashSession keeps working unchanged. The [{ }] raw-JSON button ports appendJsonRecordButton (views/timeline-render-row-cells.ts:115) / details-revision-cards.ts:49 rather than inventing a second idiom. The client never computes confidence state, never replays a patch itself, and never decides verified-vs-derived locally -- all three are read off the engine's response.

Fixture: new jfred/src/viewer_api_layer3_fixture_data.ts (one-file-per-layer convention). Every edit fixture carries a real structuredPatch ({oldStart, oldLines, newStart, newLines, lines[]}) because reconstruction_extract.ts:133-135 builds no event without one. Edits go in both the 4 hand-written sessions and the bulk loop (84 of 88 bubbles are bulk-generated). At least one pair carries edits from two sessions; one edit's hunk deliberately does not match its base so 'derived' rendering is exercised, not just 'verified'.

GATE: does not start until task #343 (L3 mockup, fixture-mode on the real layer1 page) is signed off by the user. Verify per S20's verify list: npm run typecheck, full npm test, and a headless CDP visual-checks pass (new file per S20's fixture-checks paragraph) confirming fetch-once-with-progress, instant-toggle-after, [e]/[R]checkmark rendering, replay-opens-diff-and-flashes-JSONL, the {} button, an L3-free pair rendering byte-identical to Layer 2, and the mismatched-hunk fixture showing derived not verified.

title: Engine build-out: Layer 4 script-run nodes (located, not executed)
description:
L4 is parse-only, no sandbox spawn -- executing a run's sandbox belongs to L6. Recon: plans/340-recon/L4-script-runs-located.md.

Engine must expose: the existing identification chain unchanged -- findScriptExecutionRuns (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_execution.ts:99, memoized on getCorpusState(records).scriptRuns) -> resolveScriptIndirection (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_indirection.ts:120, rewrites python3 x.py invocations to the written script's body) -> scriptCodeMayWriteFiles (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_prestate.ts:81, a boolean heuristic, not a path list). ScriptRun ({code, timestamp, cwd?, source?, toolUseId?, executorKind?}, reconstruction_script_execution.ts:28-35) has no changeId until a target is known: computeScriptExecutionChangeId(run, target) mints scriptRun:<toolUseId>. Add a 'speculative affected files for a run' helper that inverts runForTarget (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_probe.ts:34) -- scans known pair paths for basename mentions in run.code -- so a node is labelled with a filename only when the static scan actually yields one; otherwise the node still renders, showing only that a script ran, and clicking it shows the resolved script body (already solved: resolveScriptIndirection). Bash runs render identically to python runs but carry the 'never-provable' confidence state (one of the seven), ported from the existing dashed hollow-ring idiom (.kind-pre-anchor-stub, jfred/webapp/layered-styles.css:135) rather than a new style -- do not invent a second unprovable-node visual language.

New wire type WireScriptRunOf<I,P,U> + scriptRuns? on WirePairOf + a listPairLadderInstants entry, mirroring the snapshots? precedent (zero existing webapp/server references to ScriptRun today). A bracket function maps a run's instant to the nearest-before/nearest-after steps on a file's listDatedSteps so buildDiffView (jfred/webapp/layer1-diff-view.ts:29,80) can render before/after panes using the EXISTING revision kinds (describeCommitStep / describeSnapshotStep / describeDiskStep, layer1-revision-sources.ts) -- no new DiffStep type needed.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: a .n-script branch in describeNode / openNodeDrawer (jfred/webapp/layer1-drawer.ts) rendering the node label as <language icon> <filenameOfExecutedScript> (or a generated label for inline python3 -c / heredoc runs with no filename); identity is scriptRun:<toolUseId> -- ONE drawer state shared across every bubble the run touches, not one per path. All bubbles sharing a toolUseId are joined by a clickable horizontal dashed connector that itself opens the shared detail view. The client never re-resolves script indirection or re-scans for affected files -- both come from the engine.

Fixture: new jfred/src/viewer_api_layer4_fixture_data.ts. Canned script bodies cannot ride on FixtureRevisionNode (identity-only: kind/hash/version/session) -- add a branch in contentLines (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_fixture_content.ts:73) ahead of the generic per-language template fallback.

GATE: no blocking visual mockup exists for L4 (unlike L5/L6) -- gates on its spec item (next free S-number after S20, per handoff step 2) being written and signed off by the user. Layer gating is cumulative: [4] implies [3] is present.

Depends on: L4's spec item (handoff step 2) written and signed off; benefits from L3 landing first since [4] gating implies [3], but is not code-dependent on L3's implementation.

title: Engine build-out: Layer 5 branch rendering in per-file bubbles
description:
Recon: plans/340-recon/L5-branches.md. Critical finding: buildLayer1View reads NO JSONL and imports none of reconstruction_branch/graph/json (grep-verified zero hits) -- L5 needs a session-scoped second fetch, triggered on-demand, not a change to the initial view build.

Engine must expose: branch discovery is already parse-only and reusable as-is -- ConversationBranch = {tip, rewindPoint, isSurviving} (jfred/src/reconstruction_branch.ts:27-31), built via findSurvivingHead -> findWorkingTreeOwner content-signature tiebreak, collectAbandonedHeads + findRewindPoint (jfred/src/reconstruction_trunk.ts:132,:71), findStructuralRewoundBranches (jfred/src/reconstruction_fork.ts:17). Kept-vs-reverted (byte content, not a heuristic) is a composition that already exists: reconstructBranches(records, reader) (jfred/src/reconstruction_engine.ts:172-190) returns surviving FileHistory[] plus per-rewound-branch RewoundBranchHistory with reconstructed revisions; findWorkingTreeOwner (jfred/src/reconstruction_worktree.ts:38-57) decides which content owns the surviving tree by comparing rewind-moment snapshot CONTENT signatures; the branch-agnostic steps core (jfred/src/reconstruction_steps.ts:1) already models the conv-only-vs-code-rewind disk-survives-a-rewind case. L5's job is to compose these into per-node branch membership, NOT to write new comparison logic and NOT to re-derive rewind points -- MUST call absorbParallelToolCallSiblings (jfred/src/reconstruction_trunk_absorb.ts:153-160) via the existing branch-discovery path so ordinary parallel tool calls never render as fake abandoned branches.

Per DECISIONS.md: nothing branch-related runs on page load. Clicking a [3]-or-higher layer button/checkbox runs the normal page-load stages, then a ruler-resolving stage, then a stage labelled 'reconstructing branches' in the progress strip. There is NO rewind node -- a rewind renders as dimmed nodes (opacity .38, per mvp-app-mockup.html layer 8 precedent) plus a dashed elbow connector; do not add a rewind node kind. New wire field branches? on WirePairOf plus an isOrphaned/BranchRole-equivalent field per node (the old app's isOrphaned, reconstruction_json.ts:35,59 / reconstruction_tool_calls.ts, is the closest existing precedent for the flag shape, though it lives in the classic pipeline). One ruler for the whole project -- forked lanes share the trunk's ticks, no local sub-axis.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: the chosen lane-rendering variant from the L5 mockup (a separate task, per handoff step 1) -- port lane-run boundary logic (fork/end/rejoin) from the old app's flat-row computeGraphLaneRuns (webapp/views/timeline-sessions.ts:60-76) / checkNodeIsAbandonedBranchTip (:79-89) re-derived for a bubble's vertical ladder, not copied verbatim. Bubbles widen to fit more than two lanes rather than stacking or hiding. The client never classifies a branch tip, never computes rewind points, and never decides kept-vs-reverted itself.

GATE: does not start until (a) the L5 branch-rendering mockup (2-3 static HTML variants, one of them mvp-app-mockup.html layer 8) is built and the user picks a direction, per handoff step 1, and (b) that mockup's own spec/task is signed off. Lane scope (per-session columns vs conversation-wide fork tree) and whether a tie-group rectangle spans lanes are BOTH decided by the mockup choice and must not be guessed ahead of it.

Depends on: The L5 branch-rendering mockup (separate task per handoff step 1) built, reviewed, and a variant chosen by the user.

title: Engine build-out: Layer 6 on-demand script execution replay
description:
Recon: plans/340-recon/L6-script-results.md. This is the layer that actually spawns the sandbox; L4 only locates runs.

Engine must compute/expose: reuse executeRunOnce(run, records, reader, seedContent?) -> RunExecution{pre, post|undefined} (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_runs.ts:73-115) and runScriptAgainstState (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_sandbox.ts:143-172, python3 only, execSync __script__.py, 5000ms timeout, cwd remapped into a temp dir so scripts can't escape). Wire is_error into executeRunOnce (~10-15 lines per the recon's cost re-check -- ScriptRun already carries toolUseId and records is already passed in; the toolUseId -> tool_result lookup idiom already exists twice: indexToolResultsByToolUseId, jfred/src/reconstruction_git_operations.ts:154-164, and collectRenameCandidatesFromToolResult, jfred/src/reconstruction_script_renames.ts:78-89) so an 'original-failed' run (the log's own is_error:true) is told apart from a 'replay failed' or 'not replayed' run -- three of the seven confidence states. Extend getPostExecutionBeacon (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_stage.ts:35-43, currently ONLY the file-history backup timeline via backupSeedWriteFor) to the ONE unified beacon definition settled in DECISIONS.md -- file-history backup, full-file Read echo, Bash(cat FILE) result, git commit, or snapshot, nearest AFTER the run -- so L6 never verifies against a different definition of 'beacon' than L3 does. A read-only script event yields beacon-level data itself (full contents reported) -- render it as a beacon, not an absent/empty node. A mismatch between replay output and the expected beacon becomes its own 'mismatch' node kind, not the engine's current silent fallback to keeping the original event unexplained (reconstruction_script_stage.ts, the caller today silently discards a verification failure). Add the live-working-tree read as a genuinely first-ever capability (process.cwd() appears nowhere in jfred/src/ today) used ONLY to CONFIRM a beaconless script-created file -- a match promotes to verified, a mismatch or missing file changes nothing and shows no marker, because a difference is not evidence the file wasn't touched since.

Execution scope and ordering (both settled, not open): only nodes in the rendered viewport execute, and only once per node, ever -- an off-screen node scrolled into view later is already done if its run already fired. Runs execute strictly in timeline order (no concurrency to design; each run depends on file state reconstructed by earlier points). Persistence reuses the existing sandbox memo disk file (configureSandboxMemoPersistence / flushSandboxMemoToDisk, reconstruction_script_sandbox.ts:60-74, SHA-256(script+cwd+sorted pre-state) key, batched every 64 spawns) plus a new button in the GUI top-row header that clears the memo and forces every layer to recompute from scratch. Consent reuses isImpureExecutionAllowed() (jfred/src/reconstruction_exec_gate.ts) as-is -- its own comment already flags per-request gating as a documented extension point, which this task exercises for the first time via an HTTP-triggered replay.

New route: run/node id -> executeRunOnce + stage match check -> streamNdjsonBuild progress framing (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_route.ts:43-61, the existing ?progress=1 NDJSON precedent) -- 'scoped single-file GET with streamed progress' is a new composition of two existing pieces, not new machinery. New WireScriptResultOf wire type + node classes for verified/mismatch/original-failed/etc.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: a genuinely new switcher interaction -- today the layer switcher is pure CSS and never refetches (layer1-layer-toggle.ts:1,:23); L6 computing on switch, with progress, breaks that precedent deliberately and must fire from the global load bar plus the L6 execution console mockup UI (separate task). The client never spawns the sandbox itself, never compares replay output to a beacon itself, and never reads the live working tree itself.

GATE: does not start until (a) the L6 execution-console mockup (2-3 non-interactive variants, output console + cancel button, per handoff step 1) is built and a design is picked, and (b) its own task/spec item is signed off. Also depends on L4 having landed enough that scriptRun nodes and their instants already exist on the wire to attach results to.

Depends on: The L6 execution-console mockup (separate task per handoff step 1) built and a design chosen; L4 engine build-out landed so scriptRun instants exist to attach results to.

title: Engine build-out: Layer 7 remaining node types and session annotation track
description:
Recon: plans/340-recon/L7-remaining-node-types.md. Architecture note: L7 draws from the CLASSIC engine (reconstruction_*.ts, the one that already feeds the row-based old viewer), not the layered engine -- this was the settled cross-cutting data-source question, not a choice this task re-opens.

Engine must expose: every parsed RecordType (jfred/src/structures/vocabulary.ts:4-21 + parse/recordKeys.ts -- user, assistant, system, attachment with its 14 AttachmentPayloadType kinds, fileHistorySnapshot, fileHistoryDelta, lastPrompt, mode, permissionMode, bridgeSession, aiTitle, customTitle, agentName, queueOperation, forkContextRef) gets a node. The engine must supply an ignorable classification per record so the '[check] hide ignored nodes' filter (on by default at load) can hide session/meta rows without deleting them. Tool call and tool result become TWO nodes, not the classic engine's current one collapsed node (TimelineNode union, webapp/views/timeline-types.ts:216, tool-call carries scriptRun today) -- visually bracketed by a dashed connector on the webapp side, joined by shared identity on the engine side. Any layer able to resolve a presumedUserEdit gap node (listGapsBeforeVerifiedNode, jfred/src/layered_end_state.ts:24-32) -- because no nodes sit between it and its surrounding beacons -- promotes it to verified; this is a cross-layer engine rule, not L7-exclusive, and today NOTHING promotes or demotes a presumption node, so the promotion logic itself is new. Stampless records (an EnvelopeBase.timestamp is optional by design, ~124k+ records, ~18% of the real corpus, concentrated in last-prompt/permission-mode/custom-title/agent-name/bridge-session/mode/file-history-snapshot/ai-title/worktree-state/relocated/fork-context-ref) take the PREVIOUS stamped record's timestamp -- converge the three existing conflicting behaviors onto this one rule: drop (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_sessions.ts:25-27), sort-first via empty-string default (webapp/views/timeline-line-nodes.ts, webapp/views/reconstruction-coverage.ts:84-86), sort-last (jfred/src/viewer_api_records.ts:83-86). Unknown record types render as a [?] catch-all node rather than throwing -- worktree-state (124 real occurrences) and relocated (87) are ALREADY in the real logs and absent from the RecordType enum, this is not hypothetical. There is NO code-rewind node and no code-vs-conv-only inference -- confirmed against the real s7-minimal-code-restore JSONL: zero edited_text_file attachments, file-history-snapshot versions just increment, the only trace is a shared parentUuid identical to an ordinary conversation-only rewind; do not build inference logic here, this mirrors L5's 'no rewind node' decision exactly.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: user prompts and agent responses (and the ~54k non-file metadata rows) get a NEW session-level annotation track on the shared ruler rather than being duplicated onto every touched file's bubble -- layer 1 has zero non-file-scoped lane today (every content-bearing widget is per-file via buildStagePairs/buildOrphanBucket, layer1-widgets.ts:71,89; the only session-level element is the 7px renderSessionRanges bar, layer1-widgets.ts:83-92) so this track needs its own windowing before it can render ~54k+ rows at all -- genuinely new UI, no reuse precedent exists in the recon. The client never decides a record is ignorable itself, never infers a rewind kind itself, and never invents a stampless-record timestamp itself.

GATE: no blocking visual mockup is flagged for L7 in DECISIONS.md (unlike L5/L6) -- gates on its spec item (next free S-number, handoff step 2) being written and signed off by the user. The session annotation track's windowing design should be sketched in that spec item before code, since it is new UI with no existing component to extend.

Depends on: L7's spec item (handoff step 2) written and signed off; the annotation-track windowing approach should be settled in that spec item before implementation starts.

title: Engine/webapp build-out: Layer 8 node-kind show-row filtering
description:
Recon: plans/340-recon/L8-node-type-filtering.md. This layer is almost entirely webapp-side -- CSS hide-only, never a re-layout -- and is NOT itself a layer with checkboxes (L8 adds no node kind).

Must build: a new small layer1-kind-filter.ts state module mirroring the existing onlySelectedIsOn pattern, producing a CSS class/attribute toggle switcher-style -- explicitly NOT a call into filterLayer1ViewByTargets (jfred/webapp/layer1-filter.ts:100, the path-filter funnel, which re-runs relayOutLayer1View / layOutNodeLadders and physically removes rows). Generalize markMultiEventTicks (jfred/webapp/layer1-tick-files.ts:144-157) from its current single .n-snap literal to an N-kind hidden-class set, so a ruler tick where every event is a hidden kind gets hidden too, while its slot/gap stays reserved -- dead gaps are acceptable by design, they never squish (distinct from task #341's opt-in compaction button, which is a separate, explicitly deferred mechanism). The show row is a checkbox list (not radios), reading show: [check] git [check] snapshot [check] Edit ... -- built from the kinds PRESENT IN THE LOADED VIEW, matching every other filter surface in layer 1 (renderSessionPane / listVisibleSessions, layer1-sessions.ts:156-173; listFileNavEntries, layer1-filenav.ts:24-32), never a hardcoded list of every known kind. It REPLACES the static .legend swatches (layer1.html:89-96) rather than sitting beside them. Filtering applies everywhere in the GUI including the ruler -- an expanded ruler row's file list re-filters to visible kinds, it does not keep listing every event. Zero checked = show nothing, which falls straight out of the CSS-hide model. Filter state persists with the rest of the settings data (extending /api/layer1-settings) -- explicitly NO &kinds= URL parameter. Confidence state (the seven states from DECISIONS.md) is display-only and is NEVER a filter axis in the show row -- filtering is by node KIND alone.

Clicking a layer preset button [1]-[7] ticks that layer's checkboxes; the checkboxes are the single source of truth. This retires the data-layer CSS gate entirely: the one rule keyed on it (.viz-root:not([data-layer="2"]) .n-snap {display:none}, jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css:71), layer1-layer-toggle.ts (currently 32 lines, sets dataset.layer + moves .current, no refetch/re-render), layer1.html:16,40-41, tests/layer1-layer-toggle.test.ts, three visual/CDP probes (jfred/scripts/visual/mockup.ts:27, layer2-checks.ts:18,53, mockup-checks.ts:44), and jfred/docs/ui-component-glossary.md:5,27 -- all in ONE commit, per handoff step 3's separate data-layer-retirement task. This task depends on that retirement task landing first (or lands it as part of the same change if scheduling makes that cheaper) since checkboxes and the data-layer CSS gate cannot coexist without disagreeing on the same node class.

Ticking a checkbox for a kind whose data has not yet been fetched must fire that kind's engine fetch with a visible progress strip -- per the visibility-triggers-computation cross-cutting rule -- so the show row and the layer buttons share one computation trigger, not two.

GATE: gates on its spec item (handoff step 2) being written and signed off, and on the data-layer-retirement task landing. Practically most useful once several of L3/L4/L5/L6/L7's node kinds already exist to filter, but is not code-blocked on any single one of them -- it works over whatever subset of kinds has shipped.

Depends on: L8's spec item (handoff step 2) signed off; the data-layer retirement task (handoff step 3) landed first.

title: Engine build-out: Layer 9 ruler-range git export and jfred-branch commit
description:
Recon: plans/340-recon/L9-ruler-range-export.md. This is the ONLY layer that writes to git -- every existing git call in jfred/src/ today is read-only (grep-verified: zero git commit / git apply / git branch / checkout -b anywhere in src). L9 is not a layer either (adds no node kind); it is a mode you arm.

Model (settled, amends the older S16/S17 partition text): a growing prefix, not a partition. One marked range = one segment = one commit. The first commit's base is the commit chosen by a NEW ruler-base marker; each later commit's base is the current jfred-branch tip. You may stop at any time (no full-coverage requirement) but may NOT start in the middle -- chunks only extend the prefix, and a skipped stretch is absorbed into the NEXT commit with a message noting 'includes N unmarked changes', never omitted.

Engine must build: (1) generalize resolveRangeStepIndexes (jfred/webapp/layer1-diff-wash.ts:31-50, today hard-coded to exactly 2 instants) to n cuts, each snapping PER FILE at-or-before to that file's nearest VERIFIED state -- unverified refused, never pulls future content backward, and v1 restricts markers to beacon nodes only (no derived node may carry a marker, so every jfred commit is provably a beacon, and any jfred commit counts as a beacon on the NEXT pass, resolving previously-unverified stretches as the branch extends). (2) A server-side per-file-per-segment diff loop + concatenation into one git-diff, reusing exportPatch's synthetic diff --git/---/+++ header-wrapper (jfred/webapp/layer1-diff-pane.ts:140-152, currently client-side, per-file, per-pane only) moved server-side and generalized across files. (3) A new route for apply-and-commit: git apply then git commit --date per segment, in commit order, author date = the mark's instant (always a real evidenced moment under the beacon-only rule), committer date = export wall clock, commit message carrying a footnote 'reconstructed by JFRED @ <real timestamp>' plus any per-file snap-variance note. Bytes are pinned at mark time, never re-read at commit time. (4) The jfred branch: created lazily on the first commit, forked from the ruler-base marker's commit (not an orphan root, not current HEAD), immutable base (delete the branch entirely to change it -- no amend, no reset, no force-push, append-only, so the app never rewrites history it did not just create), and hidden from the repo branch picker via a ONE-LINE filter in buildLayer1RefsView (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_refs.ts:41-53, currently `git for-each-ref refs/heads` with no exclusion) so a reconstruction can never accidentally load against the synthetic branch. Also add the missing 'Branch picker' row to jfred/docs/ui-component-glossary.md, a documented gap the recon flagged.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: arming state + mark placement lives in layer1-ruler-click.ts:74-92 (today single-click only -- expand row / scroll to bubble -- no drag gesture exists yet, this task adds one). A NEW dedicated render strip beside the ruler shows jfred-branch commits with its own layout, hit-testing, and scroll sync -- nothing renders ON the ruler today, this is a genuinely new surface, not an extension of an existing one. v1 ships commit-only: no multi-file patch export UI; the existing per-file patch download stays exactly where it is (exportPatch, layer1-diff-pane.ts:140-152). The client never computes a segment's diff itself and never issues git apply/commit itself -- both go through the new server route.

GATE: no blocking visual mockup is flagged for L9 in DECISIONS.md (unlike L5/L6) -- gates on its spec item (next free S-number, handoff step 2) being written and signed off by the user. Functionally depends on beacon nodes existing on the wire (at minimum L3, since v1 markers may only land on beacon nodes) before there is anything to mark.

Depends on: L9's spec item (handoff step 2) signed off; at least L3 (beacon nodes) landed, since v1 markers may only be placed on beacon nodes.

title: Parse workflow-spawned subagent sessions (subagents/workflows/wf_*/)
description:
Add support for parsing subagent sessions spawned from a workflow, as found here: /Users/matkatmusicllc/.claude/projects/-Users-matkatmusicllc-Desktop-claude-code-src-RevEng/7fa9beca-a3ff-42e1-a182-bc136134bbf3. New on-disk shape vs plain subagents: <session>/subagents/workflows/wf_<runId>/ containing agent-*.jsonl transcripts, agent-*.meta.json sidecars, and a journal.jsonl; the session folder also has tool-results/*.txt. The engine currently only models isSidechain vocabulary (jfred/src/structures/vocabulary.ts, jfred/src/parse/recordKeys.ts) and does not discover these nested workflow agent transcripts. Extend transcript discovery/loading (loadTranscript/listEventPaths path in jfred/src/reconstruction_multi_source.ts and friends) so workflow agent JSONLs are parsed, and decide how meta.json + journal.jsonl are represented.

NOTE ON THE files LIST (added 2026-07-31, merged from a code re-check): treat it as a starting point, not a settled fence — two of the three originally-listed paths are probably the wrong sites. reconstruction_multi_source.ts only merges already-loaded record lists (dedupe, wall-clock interleave, per-session root resolution) and never walks a directory for files; and the listEventPaths cited above is in reconstruction_bound.ts and concerns FileEvent rename src/dst paths, not transcript discovery. The real recursive .jsonl walker is listSourceFilesUnder / listTranscriptFiles in jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_sources.ts, which today matches any .jsonl at any depth and would need to tell journal.jsonl (same extension, different shape) apart from a real agent-*.jsonl transcript, and decide whether to pick up agent-*.meta.json sidecars; jfred/src/parse/loadTranscript.ts is the per-file parse entry point that would special-case them. vocabulary.ts and recordKeys.ts stay plausible only if the workflow agent transcripts or their sidecars introduce record shapes/fields not yet in RecordType / the allowed top-level keys. Confirm the real edit sites before treating this list as an ownership boundary.

title: Clear JSONLs pane (#sessions) synchronously on project switch, before the new project's build starts
description:
BUG (user's words): "changing projects should clear the jsonl nav while the project is initially loading. I saw the previous list of jsonl files in the jsonl pane."

Root cause, grounded in code: loadLayer1View() in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts (lines ~172-182) synchronously clears #stage and #filenav-tree before starting the new project's build ("Clear all three before the ~10 s build: leaving the stale view up made the page read as frozen"), and calls resetSessionSelection() from jfred/webapp/layer1-sessions.ts. But resetSessionSelection() (layer1-sessions.ts:57-61) only clears in-memory state (selectedPaths.clear(), sessions = [], knownProjectPaths = new Set()) — it does NOT touch the #sessions DOM element. The JSONLs pane's DOM (#sessions, populated by renderSessionPane() in layer1-sessions.ts:156-173) is only re-rendered much later, inside renderLayer1View() (layer1-page.ts:155: void loadLayer1Sessions().then(() => renderSessionPane(redrawFiltered))), which itself runs only after the full /api/layer1-view stream resolves. So for the whole duration of the new project's build, #sessions still shows the PREVIOUS project's session rows (.session-item elements built by buildSessionItem, each showing session.file — a jsonl file name) — exactly the "previous list of jsonl files in the jsonl pane" the user saw.

Fix: make resetSessionSelection() (or the call site in loadLayer1View) also clear/re-render the #sessions DOM synchronously, the same way #filenav-tree is cleared at line 175 of layer1-page.ts — e.g. getRequiredElementById("sessions").replaceChildren() immediately in loadLayer1View, or have resetSessionSelection do it directly so every caller gets the fix.

title: Reset in-memory JSONL/file-history source-folder lists (listsByKind) when the project folder changes
description:
BUG (user's words): "changing projects should clear the jsonl sources list of the previous project's source list." This is the JSONL source pickers (modal) — distinct from the JSONLs pane covered in the sibling task on "jsonl nav"/#sessions.

Root cause, grounded in code: jfred/webapp/layer1-source-paths.ts holds listsByKind: Record<SourceKind, SourceList> (module state, SourceList = { paths: string[]; touched: boolean }) for both the "JSONL sources" list and the "File History Snapshots" list shown via the shared modal (#pathpicker/#pp-list, opened by jfred/webapp/layer1-path-picker.ts's openPicker(kind), which does draftPaths = [...readSourcePaths(kind)] — i.e. it always re-reads whatever listsByKind[kind].paths currently holds). syncSourceButtons() (layer1-source-paths.ts:76-85), called at the top of loadLayer1View() in layer1-page.ts, only re-derives a list from the current #dir project folder when touched === false. Once a list has been touched (user picked folders via the modal, or it was seeded from the URL via fillSourceBoxesFromUrl, or restored from saved settings), touched never resets to false — so navigating to a different project folder leaves listsByKind[kind].paths holding the PREVIOUS project's folder list untouched, and the picker/button counts keep showing it.

Fix: when the project folder (#dir) changes, reset listsByKind back to { paths: [], touched: false } for both kinds (mirroring the pattern resetSessionSelection() uses in layer1-sessions.ts) so syncSourceButtons() re-derives fresh defaults for the new project instead of carrying over the old project's list. Add a reset function to layer1-source-paths.ts and call it from layer1-page.ts's loadLayer1View() before syncSourceButtons() runs.

title: Aggregate nested git repos' (submodule) commit history into the timeline reconstruction
description:
FEATURE (user's words): "if a project contains submodules, include the sub-module commit history when constructing the timeline. example: I should be able to use the 'claude code src' folder as the project that I'm opening, and the repositories contained within and conversations that occurred explicitly in subfolders should be included in the timeline reconstruction. RevEng, and jfred/ folders contain their own repositories. 'claude code src' does not contain a repository." The parent project folder is NOT itself a git repo; it contains nested independent git repos (RevEng, and jfred/ nested inside RevEng) each with their own commit history and potentially their own Claude Code JSONL sessions recorded against subfolder cwd's. The engine must discover these nested repos and merge each one's git-derived timeline into one combined project timeline instead of assuming one repo per project.

This is the LARGEST of the batch of nine tasks just filed — scope carefully. Grounding against the real engine (code-checked 2026-07-31):

1. Every git-touching function in the engine hard-assumes ONE repo per project/request — there is no existing repo-discovery/walking logic to extend. jfred/src/reconstruction_overrides.ts's PathOverrides.repoDir?: Path is a single repo path (module state via setPathOverrides/getPathOverrides). jfred/src/viewer_api_repo.ts:87 resolveRepoParam(query) resolves exactly one repo query-param path. jfred/src/reconstruction_base_commit.ts's readCommitTimestamp(repoDir, baseCommit) and readCommitFileContent(repoDir, baseCommit, relativePath), and viewer_api_repo.ts's listRepoCommits(repoDir) / computeCommitPathMatch(records, repoDir, commit) all take one repoDir: Path directly — none of these are looped over multiple repos anywhere today.

2. A multi-JSONL-folder mechanism already exists and is the closest reusable scaffold for the "conversations in subfolders" half: SourceEntry = { projectsDir: Path; fileHistoryDir?: Path; root?: Path } / WireSourceEntry in reconstruction_overrides.ts (spec S3/S4b/S6), hydrated by hydrateProjectSources, merged by jfred/src/reconstruction_multi_source.ts (mergeMultiSourceRecords, computeSessionRoots, interleaveRecordsByTimestamp) and joined in reconstruction_multi_source_join.ts (joinCrossSourceFileIdentities, cloneRecordReplacingPath). Crucially, SourceEntry has NO repoDir field today — extending it with a per-source repo path is the natural seam, since the join/merge machinery for combining multiple record streams already exists; only the git-evidence side needs to become per-source.

3. There is no reconstruction_repo_walk.ts or equivalent directory-walk-for-git-roots logic anywhere in the engine. The only directory-walking code today is jfred/src/layer1_disk_walk.ts and jfred/src/layer1_repo_tree.ts (readRepoTreeAtRef), and both DELIBERATELY EXCLUDE submodule contents from the current single-repo view (stop at gitlinks; proven by jfred/tests/layer1-acceptance.test.ts's "reports no orphan for a submodule's contents" test — the real case is jfred's own 4 submodules, 10,884 files intentionally hidden). This is the opposite direction from what's needed: today submodule content is hidden from Layer 1's disk view; this feature needs the RECONSTRUCTION engine (not the Layer 1 disk-walk) to instead descend into nested .git dirs / .gitmodules entries and treat each as an independent repo with its own commit history feeding the timeline.

4. No existing submodule handling touches commit-history merging — every submodule-aware test/code path found (layer1_disk_walk.ts, layer1_repo_tree.ts, their tests) is about EXCLUDING submodule file listings from Layer 1's File Nav, not about reconstructing history from within them.

Scope for implementation: (a) new repo-discovery logic that walks a project folder for nested .git directories (at least one level deep, e.g. RevEng/.git and RevEng/jfred/.git) when the project folder itself is not a repo; (b) extend SourceEntry/WireSourceEntry with a per-entry repoDir; (c) make readCommitTimestamp, readCommitFileContent, listRepoCommits, computeCommitPathMatch (and any other single-repoDir git evidence readers) iterate per discovered repo and merge results, keyed so file paths stay in each repo's own relative-path space; (d) route JSONL sessions whose recorded cwd falls under a discovered nested repo to that repo's SourceEntry, reusing the existing multi-source join/interleave machinery for the combined chronological timeline.

title: Re-fetch and re-apply the new project's saved reveng-paths.json settings when the project folder changes
description:
BUG (user's words): "changing project folders does not load the new project's settings for the jsonl sources." Cross-reference: related to but distinct from the sibling tasks on clearing the JSONLs pane (#sessions) and clearing listsByKind on project switch — this one is specifically about re-LOADING the new project's saved server-side settings, not about clearing stale client state.

Root cause, grounded in code: restoreSavedSettings() (jfred/webapp/layer1-settings.ts:86) reads a project's persisted settings (backed by reveng-paths.json / WireProjectPaths via jfred/src/reconstruction_overrides.ts) and is only ever called ONCE, inside bootLayer1Page() (jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts:241: await restoreSavedSettings().catch(() => false)), which runs a single time at page load. When the user later changes the #dir project-folder box (via the "Open…" picker wired in jfred/webapp/layer1-sources.ts's wireFolderPickers, or by editing the field directly) and triggers a new build through loadLayer1View() (layer1-page.ts:160-198), restoreSavedSettings() is never called again — so the NEW project's saved reveng-paths.json entry (its JSONL-sources list, file-history-sources list, repo/baseCommit, etc., per jfred/webapp/app-paths-project.ts's WireProjectPaths wire shape) is never fetched or applied. The page keeps operating on whatever settings were loaded for the FIRST project at boot.

Fix: call restoreSavedSettings() again whenever the project folder changes — either from loadLayer1View() before it derives source paths (syncSourceButtons()), or from the #dir picker's afterPick callback in wireFolderPickers (layer1-sources.ts) / the #dir text input's change handler — so the newly-selected project's persisted settings are actually loaded rather than only applying at first boot.

title: Enable multi-select on the JSONL locations native folder picker
description:
FEATURE (user's words): "enable multi-select on the 'JSONL locations' native folder picker." This is the "JSONL sources" list editor: button #pick-jsonl in jfred/webapp/layer1.html opens the shared source-folder modal (#pathpicker/#pp-list, jfred/webapp/layer1-path-picker.ts), whose [+] button calls addPickedFolder() (layer1-path-picker.ts:72-88), which fetches GET /api/pick-folder (jfred/src/viewer_server.ts:135-148, handleFolderPickRequest) and adds exactly ONE returned path to the draft list per click.

Grounded mechanism: handleFolderPickRequest shells out to osascript -e 'POSIX path of (choose folder with prompt "Select folder"...)' — a native macOS AppleScript folder chooser that, as written, returns a single POSIX path. AppleScript's choose folder command supports 'with multiple selections allowed', which returns a LIST of aliases instead of one — this is a native platform capability, not something to hand-roll. The response today is { path: string } (line 147: sendJson(response, 200, { path: picked })); addPickedFolder() in layer1-path-picker.ts destructures { path } and pushes one entry into draftPaths.

Fix: add 'with multiple selections allowed' to the choose folder AppleScript call, change the result parsing to split multiple returned POSIX paths (osascript with a list result typically joins with ', ' — verify actual output format), change /api/pick-folder's response shape to a list (e.g. { paths: string[] }), and update addPickedFolder() to append every returned path (skipping ones already in draftPaths, same de-dup rule as today) instead of just one.

Note: #pick-jsonl and #pick-fh (File History Snapshots, covered by a sibling task) share this exact same modal, addPickedFolder() function, and server endpoint — implementing this fix naturally also benefits the file-history picker, but keep the two tasks and their acceptance criteria separate per the user's explicit request.

title: Prevent browser text selection during shift-click diff-range gesture on bubble title and "N commits · on disk" labels
description:
BUG (user's words): "Shift clicking the nodes causes the bubble title label and 'N commits - on disk' labels to be selected. Those labels should not be selected."

title: Engine: discover and load <sessionId>/subagents/ transcripts so fork-subagent file edits are not silently dropped
description:
Engine: descend into <sessionId>/subagents/ so file edits made inside /btw fork subagents are not silently dropped. Task 338 verified this gap and documented it in plans/task-338-findings.md. The engine never reads the subagents folder next to a session JSONL, so any Edit or Write performed by a forked subagent is invisible to the timeline. Distinct from task 362, which covers subagents/workflows/wf_* only.

VERIFIED ROOT CAUSE (from plans/task-338-findings.md): listJsonlFiles in jfred/src/viewer_api_projects.ts does a single-level readdirSync filtering on .jsonl and never recurses; scanProjects treats only the immediate children of the projects root as loose files or named projects, so a session's own <sessionId>/subagents/ folder is structurally never visited. No loader in layered_load.ts or reconstruction_cli.ts resolves forkContextRef.parentSessionId / .parentLastUuid back to a subagent file either. The parser side already works: RecordType.forkContextRef is modeled in structures/vocabulary.ts and allow-listed in parse/recordKeys.ts, so a subagents/agent-*.jsonl file would parse fine if anything fed it to loadTranscript. No test anywhere exercises loading a real subagents/agent-*.jsonl.

APPROACH RECOMMENDED BY THE FINDINGS DOC: (1) add a listSubagentTranscripts(projectDir, sessionId) helper near listJsonlFiles in viewer_api_projects.ts that finds <projectDir>/<sessionId>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl and returns them as an explicit SEPARATE source list — do not silently merge into scanProjects' per-project listing, since these are per-session not per-project. (2) In reconstruction_cli.ts / layered_load.ts, when a subagent transcript's fork-context-ref line has a parentSessionId/parentLastUuid matching the session being reconstructed, load it through the existing loadTranscript path (no parser change needed) and run its tool-use records through the normal file-event extraction in reconstruction_extract.ts, attributing resulting EditEvent/FileEvent to the tree at parentLastUuid, tagged as a sidechain — mirroring how isSidechain:true is already carried.

Note that particular fork made zero tool calls, so a fixture proving the dropped-edit case must be constructed with at least one Edit or Write in the subagent transcript.
